chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'The man performs Hajj on behalf of the woman, and the woman performs Hajj on behalf of the man.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Can a man perform Hajj on behalf of a woman and vice versa?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) affirms the mutual permissibility of gender-crossing representation in Hajj, a ruling that distinguishes Shia jurisprudence from some Sunni schools which often restrict this to specific cases like the elderly or infirm. This hadith underscores the principle of ease (yusr) in ritual obligations, allowing a healthy individual to perform Hajj for a relative who is unable to do so due to age, illness, or other valid impediments. The ruling highlights the flexibility within Shia fiqh regarding the delegation of religious duties when the primary actor is physically incapable.
